notes.title: One reader, two consumers
notes.body: src/read.ts (672 lines) produces Annotation/Screenshot/Compare models; index.ts validates with it and html.ts draws from it, so the plugin and the renderer cannot disagree about a block.

notes.title: HTML only, on purpose
notes.body: There is no vue.ts, react.ts or svelte entry: AGENTS.md says a per-framework copy would clone the whole figure template. The cost is that annotate is the one package the JSX renderers can't use.

notes.title: Geometry is resolved at one size
notes.body: place.ts fixes stamps at 15px and notes at a 420px width, then avoids overlaps (CLEAR, CORNER), so a mark's position is computed per rendered column rather than measured later.

notes.title: Styles do the linking, not the script
notes.body: styles.ts uses :has() with --ca-on so hovering or focusing a mark lights its note (and the zoomed copies) with no JS; the 40-pair cap is generated at module load.

notes.title: A 32 KB font is inlined
notes.body: font.ts embeds Caveat 400 latin as base64 in the source, so the handwriting travels in the stylesheet with no extra request; the OFL licence is in the font's name table.

notes.title: The CLI is a second, thinner surface
notes.body: cli.ts registers annotate + carousel + zoom and renders a plain page; it duplicates the docs' plugin set by hand, so a new annotate dependency has to be added there too.
